# Authorization Requirements Quality Checklist: Projects — creation, record, membership and lifecycle

**Purpose**: Validate that the authorization and write-boundary requirements are complete, unambiguous, consistent and objectively verifiable before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Predicate Definition

- [x] CHK001 Is `isAdmin` defined in this specification, or explicitly delegated to a named upstream source with a resolvable reference? [Traceability, Spec §FR-013, §FR-015]
- [x] CHK002 Is `isMember`'s full definition stated — a membership row **or** admin status — rather than left as "admits every admin implicitly"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK003 Is FR-013's "no rule this feature writes carries its own admin branch" reconcilable with FR-015's five admin-only mutators, or does "admin branch" need a definition that distinguishes a predicate from a conditional? [Clarity, Conflict, Spec §FR-013, §FR-015]
- [x] CHK004 Is it specified whether a deactivated account holding a membership row still satisfies `isMember`, or is it stated that deactivation prevents authentication and makes the question moot? [Gap, Spec §FR-045, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK005 Are the terms "member", "roster row", "membership" and "on the roster" used consistently, given FR-018 makes an admin a writer who is not on the roster? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-018, §FR-045]

## Server Enforcement and Entry Points

- [x] CHK006 Is the set of server entry points this feature adds stated as closed, so a reviewer can tell that no mutator or read escapes the predicate rule? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §FR-015, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK007 Does FR-014's "derive the project from the stored row" rule state how it applies to `createProject`, which has no stored row to derive a project from? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, §FR-015]
- [x] CHK008 Are authentication and authorization requirements stated for the as-typed key-uniqueness check, which is a server entry point that discloses the existence and name of an existing project? [Gap, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK009 Are rate-limiting or abuse requirements stated for the as-typed key check, which is called on keystrokes and enumerates the installation's key space? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK010 Are request-origin or cross-site request requirements stated for this feature's mutators, or explicitly delegated to a named inherited convention? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK011 Are refusal requirements distinguished between a route render, which FR-023 answers with the Forbidden screen, and a direct mutator call, whose refusal shape is not stated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK012 Is the requirement that `deleteProject` observes the project's status inside its own transaction stated as a functional requirement, or does it exist only as an acceptance scenario? [Traceability, Spec §FR-047, §US4-9]

## The Read Boundary

- [x] CHK013 Are unauthenticated-access requirements stated for `/projects/:projectKey/details`, or only for `/projects/new`? [Gap, Spec §FR-023, §FR-035]
- [x] CHK014 Is the identity projection used by the roster and the member picker stated as a requirement, rather than appearing only under inherited assumptions? [Traceability, Spec §FR-018, §FR-045, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK015 Is FR-017's "membership MUST NOT be used as a visibility boundary" scoped precisely enough to distinguish it from FR-008's rule that the issue-counter row is reachable from no read endpoint at all? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-017]
- [x] CHK016 Is it specified what a reader who is neither a member nor an admin may see of a member's account details on the roster? [Gap, Privacy, Spec §FR-017, §FR-018]

## Roster Semantics

- [x] CHK017 Are the picker's exclusion rules stated as a complete set — deactivated accounts, the creating admin, people already on the roster — and is it stated whether an admin absent from the roster is offered? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §FR-030, §FR-045]
- [x] CHK018 Is FR-030's exclusion of "the creating admin" reconciled with FR-045's Add member picker, which excludes people already on the roster but says nothing about the acting admin? [Consistency, Spec §FR-030, §FR-045]
- [x] CHK019 Can FR-019's "and nothing else" be objectively verified, given it enumerates assignments, comments and activity rows that do not exist until later entries? [Measurability, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK020 Is FR-046's "on their next request" backed by a stated requirement that no membership decision is cached in a session or token? [Clarity, Spec §FR-046, §SC-007]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements stated for a membership revoked between a mutator's predicate check and its write within the same request? [Gap, Coverage, Concurrency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-020]

## Refusal Presentation

- [x] CHK022 Is "on the next render" in FR-020 defined by an observable trigger, so a reviewer can tell when the obligation has been met? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK023 Is the required content of an inline reason specified consistently, given US2 names the project to be added to while FR-041 and FR-047 imply role- and status-based reasons? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §FR-041, §FR-047]
- [x] CHK024 Do FR-038's requirement to name "what failed and why" and the obligation to keep server-side detail out of client responses conflict for an authorization refusal? [Conflict, Spec §FR-021, §FR-038]
- [x] CHK025 Is FR-021's "every action a user cannot take on these screens" bounded to an enumerable set of controls, or is it open-ended? [Measurability, Spec §FR-021, §SC-015]
- [x] CHK026 Is it specified whether the reason text must be programmatically associated with the control it disables, rather than merely rendered near it? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-021]

## Scenario and Edge Coverage

- [x] CHK027 Are requirements stated for the recovery path after an authorization refusal — what the user is expected to do next, and whether any state is retained? [Gap, Recovery, Spec §FR-038, §FR-041]
- [x] CHK028 Are requirements stated for an admin whose own admin status is revoked mid-session while a project screen is open? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK029 Is it specified whether authorization refusals produce any server-side record in this feature, or is the absence of one stated as deliberate given activity is deferred? [Gap, Observability, Spec §FR-019, §Out of Scope]
- [x] CHK030 Do SC-014 and SC-015 together cover every authorization outcome the functional requirements name, or is a measurable criterion missing for the mutator-level refusals? [Coverage, Traceability, Spec §SC-014, §SC-015]

## Resolution log

Recorded 2026-08-31 at the reviewer's request, after walking every item against
[`docs/product/specifications.md`](../../../docs/product/specifications.md),
[`docs/product/requirements-index.md`](../../../docs/product/requirements-index.md),
[`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md) and this feature's own plan artifacts.

**Covered** — the requirement was already answered, in this spec or in a document it inherits from; the
citation is given and nothing changed. **Resolved** — the gap was real and a change was made; what
changed is named.

- **CHK001** · *Covered* — §2 states `isAdmin(user) = user.role === 'admin'` as code. §6 adds that `role` is read from the user row on every request rather than cached in a token.
- **CHK002** · *Covered* — §2 states it in full: `isMember(user, project) = isAdmin(user) || hasProjectMemberRow(project.id, user.id)`.
- **CHK003** · *Covered* — No conflict. §2's rule is about *downstream rules* — "no downstream rule needs an `|| isAdmin` branch" — not about which predicate a mutator selects. FR-015 selects a predicate; it does not branch inside one.
- **CHK004** · *Covered* — Moot, and the source says why: §6 has deactivation revoke writes immediately and delete every session row, so a deactivated account never reaches the predicate. §3.9 confirms memberships are retained for reactivation.
- **CHK005** · *Covered* — §2 draws the distinction in terms — "Membership predicates include admins; membership lists do not" — and FR-013 and FR-018 mirror it.
- **CHK006** · *Resolved* — FR-026 now names the as-typed key check as a server entry point in its own right and gives it a predicate, closing the set at six mutators plus one authorizing read.
- **CHK007** · *Resolved* — FR-014 now scopes the derived-project rule to project-scoped predicates, as §2 does, and states that `createProject` requires `isAdmin`, which takes no project.
- **CHK008** · *Resolved* — FR-026: the check requires `isAdmin`, matching the screen that calls it, because its answer names an existing project.
- **CHK009** · *Resolved* — Recorded as a stated non-requirement under *Assumptions*: no throttle, because the endpoint is admin-only and discloses to an admin only what the admin-only screen already shows. §6's throttle covers sign-in and reset alone.
- **CHK010** · *Covered* — §6: "`SameSite=Lax` plus an origin check on every mutating request." Now cited in *Inherited constraints* so a reader of this document finds it.
- **CHK011** · *Covered* — Both shapes are specified: FR-023 with §3.11 fixes the route render (Forbidden inside the shell), and FR-014 with §4's *Rejected write* row fixes the call (typed refusal, toast naming the rule).
- **CHK012** · *Resolved* — FR-047 now requires the status read inside the delete's own transaction under a row lock, on the precedent of §5 invariant 13.
- **CHK013** · *Covered* — §3.11 states the rule for every authenticated route, not only this one: "an unauthenticated request to an authenticated route redirects to `/signin` and never reaches this screen."
- **CHK014** · *Covered* — §5's *Read boundary* defines `publicUser` and requires every endpoint to reuse it. *Inherited constraints* is the correct home for a convention this feature does not own.
- **CHK015** · *Covered* — §5's *Read boundary* lists exactly which tables are unreachable — `issue_counter` among them — and makes everything else readable by any signed-in user. The rules do not overlap.
- **CHK016** · *Covered* — `publicUser` is enumerated in §5: `id, first_name, last_name, avatar_url, role, job_title, deactivated_at`. The contact fields sit in `accountUser`, which only Accounts and Profile use.
- **CHK017** · *Resolved* — FR-045 now states the Add member picker does not exclude the acting admin, who may add themselves to a roster they are not on.
- **CHK018** · *Resolved* — The same amendment names the asymmetry with FR-030 as deliberate: the create form excludes the creating admin because the project does not yet exist to be joined.
- **CHK019** · *Covered* — §2 states the general rule — "Removing someone from a project does nothing else" — and the enumeration illustrates it. The mutator deletes one row, which is verifiable today.
- **CHK020** · *Covered* — §6: "Nothing about identity or membership is cached anywhere — membership is read per mutation — so there is no stale-claim window." Now cited in *Inherited constraints*.
- **CHK021** · *Resolved* — FR-014 now requires the project-scoped predicate to be evaluated inside the write's own transaction, so a concurrent revocation is ordered either before the check or after the write, never between; `isAdmin` stays outside it, being the actor's own role rather than a row the write races with. [`contracts/mutators.md`](../contracts/mutators.md) places it at step 5b and T043 asserts it.
- **CHK022** · *Covered* — §4's *Stale after navigation* row defines the mechanism: "A revisited screen re-queries the server; nothing renders from a client cache." Now cited in *Inherited constraints*.
- **CHK023** · *Covered* — §4's *Rejected write* row gives the canonical form — "Only project members can edit issues in Website Redesign" — the rule and the project, on every surface.
- **CHK024** · *Covered* — No conflict. §4's own example names the authorization rule; AGENTS.md's generic-message rule concerns SQL, stack traces and configuration. Different things.
- **CHK025** · *Resolved* — FR-021 now carries §2's navigation exception, and FR-022 says the sidebar `+` is hidden from a non-admin rather than rendered disabled.
- **CHK026** · *Covered* — AGENTS.md → React Aria Components: "Every control needs an accessible name, a visible focus indicator, and error text associated with the control." §7 delegates the semantics wholesale.
- **CHK027** · *Covered* — §4's *Rejected write* and *Permission-disabled* rows: the change rolls back and the reason states what would have to be true. There is no further step to specify.
- **CHK028** · *Covered* — §2's "Losing write access mid-session" rule is role-agnostic, §6 reads `role` from the row every request, and §2's last-active-admin invariant bounds the case. FR-020 restates it.
- **CHK029** · *Covered* — Deliberate silence upstream: §2's activity type list holds no refusal type and §6 records only `auth_attempt`, for sign-in and reset. *Out of Scope* defers all activity to R7.
- **CHK030** · *Resolved* — SC-016 added — every mutator refuses a caller who fails its predicate on 100% of calls that bypass the client, naming the rule rather than the stored row.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
